entities.summary: Lazare de Baïf (1496–1547) was a French diplomat and humanist. He served as the French ambassador to Venice from 1521 to 1524, where he played a crucial role in securing the release of the Venetian ambassador to France. De Baïf's diplomatic efforts also led to the establishment of a cultural exchange program between France and Italy. His legacy as a diplomat and humanist has endured, with his son Jean-Antoine de Baïf becoming a prominent figure in Venetian society. De Baïf's contributions to the French Renaissance were significant, and his work continues to be studied by scholars today. The impact of his diplomatic efforts can be seen in the strengthening of relations between France and Italy during the 16th century. As a key figure in the French Renaissance, de Baïf's influence extended beyond the realm of diplomacy, shaping the cultural and intellectual landscape of 16th-century Europe. In 1547, de Baïf passed away, leaving behind a legacy that would be remembered for centuries to come.
